findings.title: Child-taking as a creature–Creator boundary
findings.claim: The focus joins the not-befitting relation to al-Rahman with a child as the object of taking. In 26:211, a separate inability clause follows a not-befitting clause; in 39:4, the hypothetical child is placed among what God creates; and 19:30 describes the human speaker as God's servant. These wider contacts let the denial read as a boundary against assigning a creaturely child relation to the Creator, beyond a bare prohibition.
findings.mechanism: The focus's taking-for-oneself verb and child object meet 39:4's creation frame, while its negated suitability predicate meets 26:211's independent capacity denial. The same-surah description at 19:30 adds a servant identity for the human figure. Together these triggers change the relation from a rule about taking into a creator–creature incompatibility.
findings.reader_payoff: The distinction between a child's existence and a claim of divine parentage becomes visible: the child remains a created person, while the focus marks the attributed relation as unfitting.
findings.containment: The focus's ordinary child or offspring sense remains intact. The wider contacts do not make walad mean only an adopted child, identify every child with the figure in 19:30, or supply lexical analysis of the target verses.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches and the named connections support a bounded structural relation. The target Arabic is supplied, but target morphology is not, so the reading stays at the verse-relation level.

findings.title: Mercy as a relation to humankind
findings.claim: The focus's name al-Rahman stands beside the wider description of a sign as وَرَحْمَةًۭ مِّنَّا ('and a mercy from Us'). This contact lets the name resonate with divine beneficence reaching people through a sign, alongside the focus's denial of divine offspring.
findings.mechanism: The focus's divine name is the carrier; the distinct phrase 'a mercy from Us' at 19:21 is the trigger. Their supplied wording meets through the mercy branch, changing al-Rahman from only a criterion in the focus's negative relation into a name that also resonates with active benefit reaching creation.
findings.reader_payoff: A second relation to humankind becomes perceptible: the wider passage can describe a human figure as a sign and mercy from God while the focus denies child-taking.
findings.containment: This is a verse-level resonance. It does not make al-Rahman a corporeal or womb term, nor does it identify the focus's indefinite child as only the figure described at 19:21.

epistemic.reason: The exact target Arabic and focus occurrence are supplied, but the connection is a reciprocal nomination and target morphology is absent; the claim is limited to the visible mercy wording and its contextual relation.
